economy.summary: His campaign platform says the minimum wage must be raised to $15 an hour, which he says would lift pay for workers and reverse decades of growing pay inequality. He also supports strategic investments and responsible economic development projects in the district.
economy.short: Supports raising minimum wage to $15; supports economic development investments.

abortion.summary: Describes himself as 100% pro-choice, saying neither state nor federal government has any right to tell a woman what she can or cannot do on reproductive rights. He voted against bills restricting abortion, including a 20-week ban, and co-sponsored a bill to bar cooperation with out-of-state abortion investigations.
abortion.short: Describes himself as 100% pro-choice; voted against abortion restrictions.

education.summary: Chairs the House Education Committee. He authored legislation, now in the school code, requiring weekly on-camera wellness checks for cyber charter students, saying students should learn in a safe and healthy environment, and defended giving last year's cyber charter funding changes a year or two to show their impact.
education.short: Education Committee chair; authored cyber charter student wellness-check law.

energy.summary: Sponsored House Bill 1842 to create a community solar program letting customers subscribe to shared solar facilities, calling it a win for renewable energy access, the grid, the environment, and jobs. He reintroduced community solar legislation that passed the House in 2026 as part of the governor's energy plan.
energy.short: Sponsors community solar legislation; supports renewable energy access.

guns.summary: Supports stricter firearms regulations: he co-sponsored a bill to ban high-capacity semi-automatic weapons, co-sponsored universal background checks for gun-show purchases, supported safe storage requirements, and voted against permitless concealed carry.
guns.short: Supports background checks, safe storage; opposed permitless concealed carry.
